description: We are the fire marshals of Africa. We make the continent better one fire at a time!
summary: We developed a multi-tiered satellite harmonization framework that standardizes 20 years of MODIS and VIIRS fire observations into a single, continuous historical record. It works by mapping detections onto equal-area grids, normalizing activity rates with clear-sky observation logs, applying area-scaled detectability floors, and translating raw sensor physics into calibrated probabilities while preserving small burns in dedicated layers. This is vital because it prevents decision-makers from mistaking improved satellite vision for an actual spike in wildfires, unlocking trustworthy multi-decadal trends with transparent uncertainty bounds.
details:
African forests and agriculture represent a big part of the African economy. Fire hazards happening in Africa may be a burden on the economy; an example of that is the fire that happened in KwaZulu-Natal in South Africa in 2024.

Our project is a web app built with Flask as a prototype (under development and continuous improvements/maintenance) that serves as a gift to Earth that saves it from those fires. It targets wildfire managers and forest managers in Africa and worldwide, offering them a centralized platform where they can have access to historical fire activities and hotspots linked with timelines, after integrating the framework of harmonization of different sensor databases from NASA FIRMS (MODIS and VIIRS).

It is open to both regular users and fire managers, as they can select a specific area/forest and get access to analysis that can inform their decisions and predictions about any unusual trends that can trigger an upcoming fire. More functionalities are coming soon for fire managers as they get access to a centralized, customizable account creation where they choose their area of focus and the platform serves as their workspace and investigation workspace.

Our team has also tested the app with different screen readers (NVDA/JAWS/Narrator) to ensure it's fully accessible and compliant with the WCAG 2.2 framework. It is fully built using Flask, and other dependencies are clearly articulated in requirements.txt as Python extensions.
